bugs.error_message: Anonymous-user pixel popup showed the full run metadata dl (acquisition window, location, OPERA products, frame, run ID, layer range, bbox, use-bbox button) plus a disclaimer and login-hint sentence, appended after all of it. User wanted just the pixel value and a plain-language rate explanation, nothing else.
bugs.root_cause: Initial implementation appended a new PixelInterpretation block onto the existing RunDetailsPopup content instead of replacing it for the !isAuthed case — so anonymous users saw the full authed-user metadata dump plus the new block, not a simplified view.
bugs.fix: RunDetailsPopup now branches early on !isAuthed and renders a separate minimal PixelValuePopup (title + sampled value + layerContext what/sign explanation only); the full metadata/bbox/button view is now authed-only, unchanged from before this feature.

bugs.error_message: User clicked a visibly-colored Displacement pixel and the popup said 'Exact value unavailable for this preview layer' — user reported 'there's clearly data there but we can't get the value, something is broken.'
bugs.root_cause: Most displacement runs render via the cheap pre-rendered PNG overlay path (ImageOverlay), not StacCogLayer — a flat image with no per-pixel access from the browser, so the original click handler for that path never sampled anything. The real COG asset is still published alongside the overlay (itemLayers returns both a 'cog' and an 'overlay' entry), it just wasn't used for sampling.
bugs.fix: Added sampleCogValueAt(href, lat, lon) to pixelSample.js — lazily parses just the underlying COG (cached per href) and samples it on demand. Wired into the ImageOverlay click handler (updates the open popup's value once resolved) and into the address-search probe effect (checks overlay-backed runs via bbox after the registered-sampler COG layers). Regression caught during this fix: a first pass statically imported `georaster` in pixelSample.js, which pulled the ~580KB georaster bundle out of its lazy chunk into the main bundle (caught via `npm run build` chunk output before shipping) — fixed by dynamic-importing it the same way StacCogLayer already does.

bugs.error_message: User: 'Clicking doesn't work to show up a popup at all.' Broke for every run after 'Render the Cogs' made StacCogLayer the only displacement rendering path (previously masked because most displacement runs used ImageOverlay instead).
bugs.root_cause: georaster-layer-for-leaflet@4.1.2 (checked both dist entry points actually resolved by package.json's main/module fields) is a plain L.GridLayer.extend({...}) with ZERO click/interactive-target support — it never calls Leaflet's addInteractiveTarget and never fires 'click'/'contextmenu' on the layer instance. StacCogLayer.jsx's `layer.on('click', ...)` therefore never fired from a real user click; it only appeared to work because velocity (which always used StacCogLayer) was rarely tested and displacement usually rendered via ImageOverlay instead (react-leaflet's own working event wiring).
bugs.fix: Moved real interactivity from the (non-functional) layer-level Leaflet event to the map level: StacResults.jsx now attaches `click`/`contextmenu` via `useMapEvents`, reusing the existing `samplersRef` registry (bounds + sampleAt per rendered layer, same mechanism already built for the address-search probe) via a new shared `findSampledRunAt(lat, lon)` helper (topmost-registered-first). Removed the dead onClick/onContextMenu props + layer.on(...) wiring from StacCogLayer.jsx entirely rather than leave misleading code that looks functional but isn't. Verified with a real Playwright/Chromium click (not just a synthetic function call) against a minimal harness mounting the actual StacCogLayer + a local range-request-capable COG server: click reached useMapEvents({click}), bounds.contains() matched, and sampleAt() returned the exact GDAL ground-truth value.

bugs.error_message: User: 'Also are all images normalized across the maximum range of values across all images? They should be.' — implicitly reporting they weren't.
bugs.root_cause: combinedRange(dispRuns/velocityRuns, kind) computes the min/max across every currently-shown run of a kind, but that value was only ever passed to RasterLegend (the panel's legend labels) — each individual StacCogLayer was colored using its OWN per-run range (cog.range/vel.range) via pixelValuesToColorFn. So the legend showed one scale while the map rendered a different scale per run, and colors weren't comparable between simultaneously-displayed runs.
bugs.fix: Added displacementColorRange/velocityColorRange ({vmin, vmax} built from the same combinedRange() legend value) and pass that into StacCogLayer's `range` prop for both displacement and velocity, falling back to the per-run range only if no combined range exists (e.g. no run in view carries range metadata at all).
